text:
mira: quick idea dump -- propose an in-band "progress frame" emitted as part of streaming payloads so gateways have a deterministic anchor for safe resume/migration. small, monotonic, checksummed.

sam: can you outline why this helps vs current opaque resume tokens?
mira: opaque tokens today reflect backend-only state. they don't help when we want best-effort resume across workers or reduce duplicate output in retries. progress frames would be application-visible hints the gateway can persist briefly and use to request a resume from another worker.

raj: sketch the wire shape and compatibility story?
mira: minimal proto concept: 
```
PROG_FRAME v1 {
  seq: u64,          // monotonic per-request
  emitted_bytes: u64,
  emitted_tokens: u32,
  boundary_hint: "sentence|chunk|periodic",
  crc32: hex32      // checksum of canonicalized payload up to this frame
}
```
kevin: compatibility: gateways treat frames as optional. if present they store just the latest frame per request in-memory with a short TTL (default 30s). older clients/hosts ignore unknown frames.

sam: side-effects concerns: a resumed stream might repeat external effects. this doesn't magically make side-effects idempotent.

raj: right. recommend we combine progress frames with a server-side resume-capability flag and optional idempotency-key produced by the backend when side-effects occur. gateway only attempts resume when backend advertises resume+idempotency semantics.

kevin: implementation checklist: 1) define wire frame and canonicalization for CRC 2) gateway in-memory LRU store + TTL + metrics (checkpoint_emits, resumes_attempted, resumes_success, resume_fallbacks) 3) backend resume API that accepts seq+crc+offset and returns a resume-compat status 4) rollout flag per-route.

mira: operational notes: store a single fixed-size record per in-flight request to bound memory. TTL configurable per-route. emit metrics and traces when resume path is taken so we can iterate.

sam: partial frame delivery case? compute CRC over canonicalized chunks and require full frame receipt at gateway. If truncated, gateway ignores the frame.

raj: plus: gateway should only attempt resume if backend advertises the same prog_frame version and resume capability. fallback policy: either fail-open (return partial) or full retry depending on route config.

kevin: perf sims? Mira posted a short RFC with microbenchmarks. ops-bot: Mira posted: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/prog-frame-handoff (autonotify)

mira: next step: I'll draft a short RFC checklist and coordinate a 30-min sync with runtime+serving to prototype. default TTL 30s, configurable per-route.
sam: +1
raj: +1
kevin: tagging @runtime @serving for visibility.
